5.1.6. Supplemental analysis
As described earlier, control conditions were included for Task A
and Task B framing to provide further insights about the nature of
the results presented above. Therefore, we also subjected partici-
pants’ attention residue to a 3 (Task A frame) = 3 (Task B frame)
ANCOVA. As in the analysis reported above, reaction times to the
neutral words were used as covariate to capture individual base
rate in reaction times. Consistent with Hypothesis 1, and as
reported in Table 3, the analysis of attention residue revealed a
signiﬁcant main effect of Task A framing (F(2,205) = 7.08, p < 0.01,
g2 = 0.07). In particular, those assigned to Task A promotion fram-
ing exhibited less attention residue as compared to those assigned
to Task A control framing (F(1,144) = 5.64, p < 0.05, g2 = 0.04), as
shown in Table 2. By contrast, there was no signiﬁcant difference
in attention residue between Task A prevention and Task A control
framings (p = 0.77). This pattern of results suggests that the
differences in attention residue between Task A promotion and
Task A prevention framings results from a promotion focus reduc-
